original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Exhaust the 15,680 ordered P112 ten-term factorizations D=[X,XU], T=[X(I−VU^T),XV], where U and V are ordered pairs of distinct Walsh characters and the two rank-two bases use identity or one of four elementary unimodular shears; compute every exact pairing-rank profile and the charged-center packing ceiling.
scope_change_reason: The selected complex-rank-shape card asks for a fixed support alphabet whose profile could improve the local moment. The broad coupled rank-two P112 class is open after PR1197, but PR1923 and PR2022 added close ten-term results. This contribution narrows to an explicit asymmetric character-plane family plus four non-free basis changes, preserving the exact decoder identity while varying the supports. The optimistic ten-rank-one budget cleared the 5% gate, so the finite construction search was worth running. Its completed exact census is negative; it does not claim a universal floor.
bottleneck_link: Replacing the selected eight rank-8 center terms (invoice 64) could change both the local rank distribution and the 64-per-call center charge. The exact Walsh-shear invoices are 82, and their favorable packing ceiling is below the selected word ceiling; no center or recursive saving results.
stop_rule: Completed all 15,680 ordered character-pair/basis tuples in the declared five-basis domain, including exact identities, all term costs, the profile census, ceiling pricing, and mutation controls. No further speculative pivot in this cycle.
evidence: verify.py regenerates RESULT.json. All 15,680 parameter tuples have profile {8:8,9:2}, invoice 82, and ceiling interval [834274164361/1000000000000000, 417137082181/500000000000000], below both the incumbent ceiling and 5% gate. Coefficient identities and UV invariance are exact; every rank is cross-checked by a second implementation. Positive full-matrix and negative mutation controls pass.
author: Cinna
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, derivation, implementation, exact verification, cost analysis, and writing. No independent human review or proof-assistant verification is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can arbitrary full-rank rational or real U,V with overlapping coefficient support produce a lower recursive profile than this finite Walsh-shear family?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR1197 leaves the coupled rank-two case open; a lower center invoice and rank histogram could change the complex-side packing ceiling.
open_questions.first_step: Classify support strata of U,V and test rational points on strata allowing cancellation, then compute the full support-pairing profile and charge the frame/restoration interface.
open_questions.blocked_by: The support pattern varies over continuous algebraic loci; this finite five-basis enumeration does not bound the whole coupled class.

method: Enumerate all 56 ordered distinct Walsh-character pairs independently for U and V. For each of identity, E12(+1), E12(−1), E21(+1), and E21(−1), set U_new=U M and V_new=V M^{-T}; verify U_new V_new^T=UV^T and the 8-dimensional factor identity exactly. Compute all ten support-pairing ranks with binary elimination, cross-check each against the pinned P112 geometry routine, census profiles, and price each profile with the pinned exact ceiling implementation.
nearest_overlap: PR1197 leaves the coupled full-rank overlapping-support case open and includes this subfamily. PR1923 searches a fixed symmetric witness Householder orbit (invoice 82). PR2022 reports a broader at-most-eleven-total floor and cost-40 witnesses for its fixed decoder. This work adds only a profile census for an asymmetric finite subfamily. PR2021 is masked completion rank, not this all-pairs factor invoice.
favorable_budget: A hypothetical ten-rank-one center invoice gives a ceiling near 0.004256765, above the selected 5% threshold 0.001774557. Actual domain census: ten-term histogram {8:8,9:2}, center 82; selected noncenter local mass 5522 is retained, giving ceiling upper 0.000834274164362. The ceiling allows fractional rank-51 idle packing and waives source, frame, adapter, restoration, hosting, precision, and interface costs.
